chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abū Ḥamza al-Thumālī, from his father, raising it to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn (peace be upon him) said in his sermon: 'I seek refuge with Allah from the sins that hasten destruction.' So ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Kawwāʾ al-Yashkurī stood up to him and said: 'O Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Can there be sins that hasten destruction?' He said: 'Yes, woe to you, it is severing the womb (kinship). Indeed, the people of the household may gather and cooperate with one another while they are immoral, yet Allah grants them sustenance; and indeed, the people of the household may separate and cut off one another, yet Allah deprives them while they are pious.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific sin that hastens destruction according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kāfī, transmitted through the chain of Abū Ḥamza al-Thumāli, underscores severing kinship (qaṭīʿat al-raḥim) as a specific sin that accelerates divine punishment. It illustrates a profound theological paradox where unity among the unjust preserves their sustenance, whereas discord among the righteous leads to deprivation, emphasizing the communal weight of kinship ties in Shia ethical thought.
